graph.closure_explanation: Theorem 2 (Th1) is proved from Lemma 5 (Lm5) alone (line 445) plus the elementary induction on beta_k. Lemma 5's statement uses DOBOC-K (Algorithm 2 and the DOBOC-K distributed-implementation lemma, i.e. source Lemma 3, recorded as the algorithm node ALG), a = M + 2(1-w_min)/lambda, F and x_*; its proof uses the centralized form of DOBOC-K (an internal algebraic step), Proposition 1 (pp1, eigenvalue bounds of grad^2 F), Lemma 4 (Lm4) and the inequalities (mu), (L) via (key1), (key2) (internal derivations). Lemma 4 uses the Taylor expansion error of the C^2 local functions (DTAY, derived). Symmetry of grad^2 F (DSYM, derived) is implicit in the eigenvalue arguments. The minimum point x_* is presupposed (line 345); DMIN (derived) establishes its existence from (mu). DEXEC (derived) links the template execution (one oracle call per outer iteration) to the iterates. Excluded: Theorem 1 (superlinear rate of DOBOC, the K = k variant; not used by Theorem 2), Lemma 2 (Lm2, heuristic approximation motivating the algorithm), the DOBOC distributed-implementation lemma and Remark (hsf) (about DOBOC, not DOBOC-K), the optimal-control derivation (OCP, conlaw, iteration relation) and the citations [mokhtari2016network] (Proposition 1 is stated in the paper and formalized here), [apostol1991calculus] (Taylor expansion, formalized as DTAY), [mitrinovic2013classical] (Bernoulli inequality, an internal proof step). The only convergence result in the closure is Theorem 2; all other results are supporting. Fresh interface correction reuses the accepted mathematical dependency closure after new independent review, retaining the analytic theorem and its disclosed exponent correction. The public result derives a priori tuning and a logarithmic epsilon-budget, preserves the fixed inner-K method family, and measures one all-agent gradient/Hessian reply per outer update. It makes no unpenalized-consensus accuracy or primitive communication-count claim.
